speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the history. Given your age, sun exposure, and history of diabetes, are the lesions on your hand raised and scaly, or more like flat, rough patches? Also, have they appeared suddenly or been present for a long time?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is The presence of a rough, scaly, sandpaper-like plaque on the left dorsal hand. I also have No tenderness, No pain.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Actinic Keratosis. The description of a rough, scaly, sandpaper-like plaque on the sun-exposed dorsal hand in a 65-year-old female is classic for actinic keratosis. I will proceed with a visual examination to confirm the diagnosis and rule out squamous cell carcinoma.
